name: Al-Fatihah
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih Muslim 395 (Hadith Qudsi of the Halved Prayer)
historical_context: Revealed in Mecca at the inception of mandatory congregational Salah. Whenever the Prophet prayed, the dialogue of divine communion was instituted as the Mother of the Book.
key_events: Instituted as the compulsory pillar of every Rak'ah in prayer
The divine dialogue: "Qasamtu as-salata bayni wa bayna 'abdi nisfayn"

name: Al-Baqarah
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 40 (Qiblah Shift toward the Ka'bah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4512 (Statutes of Fasting in Ramadan)
Sahih Muslim 125 (Descent of the Concluding Verses)
historical_context: Revealed over the entire Medinan era. Encompasses over 40 distinct verified historical triggers establishing the constitutional, economic, and liturgical foundation of the Muslim Ummah.
key_events: Shift of Qiblah from Jerusalem to Mecca after 16-17 months (Bukhari 40)
Institutionalization of Ramadan fasting replacing Ashura (Bukhari 4512)
Abolition of pre-Islamic usury and debt cancellation (Bukhari 4541)
The Night Journey revelation of the last two verses (Sahih Muslim 125)

name: Ali-Imran
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4380 (The Christian Delegation of Najran)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4066 (The Battle of Uhud, Verses 121-180)
historical_context: Dominated by two momentous historical crises: the ideological theological debate with the 60-member Christian delegation from Najran, and the profound trauma and military trial of the Battle of Uhud (Shawwal 3 AH).
key_events: The Christian Delegation of Najran and invocation of Mubahalah (Bukhari 4380)
The Battle of Uhud, archers deserting the ridge, and martyrdom of 70 Sahabah
Divine comfort following the rumor of the Prophet's death at Uhud

name: An-Nisa
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih Muslim 1748 (Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi's Widows & Daughters)
historical_context: Revealed largely in the aftermath of Uhud to protect the vulnerable: hundreds of orphans, widowed households, mandatory fixed female inheritance shares, and military treaties.
key_events: Protection of female orphans' estates from predatory guardians (Bukhari 4574)
The widows of Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi' establishing fixed Qur'anic inheritance
Statutes of Tayammum and fear prayer during military expeditions

name: Al-Ma'idah
historical_context: Among the final revelations descended between Treaty of Hudaibiyah (6 AH) and the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH), concluding dietary laws, international covenants, and the absolute perfection of Islam.
key_events: Jewish debate with Umar regarding "Today I have perfected your religion"
Final, uncompromising prohibition of alcohol and gambling (Bukhari 4616)
Treaty jurisprudence and judicial integrity

name: Al-An'am
historical_context: Descended almost entirely all at once in Mecca by night, escorted by 70,000 angels glorifying Allah in cosmic majestic celebration of pure monotheism (Tawhid).
key_events: Descent of pure Tawhid and refutation of polytheistic cosmological myths
Minor verse-level response to pagans disputing carrion vs slaughtered meat

name: Al-A'raf
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih Muslim 3028 (Naked Tawaf around the Ka'bah)
historical_context: Meccan revelation addressing the primordial history of mankind, with specific passages triggered by pagan customs such as performing Tawaf naked around the Ka'bah.
key_events: Abolition of the pagan custom of stripping naked for circumambulation
Descent of "Khudhoo zeenatakum 'inda kulli masjid" (Wear your adornment)

name: Al-Anfal
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4882 (Dispute Over the Spoils of Badr)
Sahih Muslim 1748 (Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas & Sword of Badr)
historical_context: Known as "Surat Badr". Revealed in Shawwal 2 AH directly following the Battle of Badr, arbitrating the dispute over military spoils (Anfal), captive ransoms, and angelic descent.
key_events: Young warriors vs veteran guard disputing the distribution of spoils
Divine decree placing all spoils under Allah and His Messenger
The casting of the handful of pebbles routing the pagan lines

name: At-Tawbah
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4418 (The Three Who Stayed Behind)
Sahih Muslim 2769 (Repentance of Ka'b ibn Malik)
historical_context: Revealed in late 9 AH regarding the grueling Expedition to Tabuk, exposing the 80 hypocrites, establishing Bara'ah (dissociation from treaty-breakers), and accepting Ka'b's repentance.
key_events: Ali proclaiming the declaration of Bara'ah at the Hajj of 9 AH
Exposing the subversive counter-mosque (Masjid al-Dirar) built by hypocrites
The fifty-day social boycott and joyous divine pardon of Ka'b ibn Malik

name: Yunus
historical_context: Middle Meccan revelation focusing on celestial signs, the maritime storm, and the preservation of Pharaoh's body; minor responses to pagans demanding an altered Qur'an.
key_events: Spontaneous revelation on cosmic tawhid and the prophetic destiny of Yunus
Refutation of polytheists saying: "Bring a Qur'an other than this or alter it"

name: Hud
historical_context: Monumental Meccan prophetic chronicle (Noah, Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, Moses). Contains Ayah 114 revealed for a remorseful companion seeking expiation for physical impropriety.
key_events: Descent of "Good deeds wipe out evil deeds" following the companion's confession
Prophetic steadfastness: "Fastaqim kama umirta" (Stand firm as commanded)

name: Yusuf
historical_context: Revealed in its entirety as a unified cinematic narrative during the Year of Sorrow (following the deaths of Khadijah and Abu Talib) to comfort the Prophet's grief-stricken heart; no authentic worldly sabab.
key_events: Spontaneous narrative solace detailing Joseph's rise from the pit to the palace
Classical consensus: Revealed Ibtida'an as "Ahsan al-Qasas"

name: Ar-Ra'd
historical_context: Exposition on cosmic doxology, thunderous praise, and heart certainty; passages revealed concerning the conspiracy of 'Amir ibn at-Tufayl and Arbad ibn Qays who were struck by lightning.
key_events: Arbad ibn Qays struck by a lightning bolt after threatening the Prophet
Descent of "Wa yursilu as-sawa'iqa fa-yuseebu biha man yashaa'"

name: Ibrahim
historical_context: Spontaneous Meccan discourse on the parables of the Pure Tree vs the Rotten Tree, Satan's sermon in Hell, and the patriarchal prayer of Ibrahim at the uncultivated valley of Mecca.
key_events: Cosmic contrast between Kalimah Tayyibah and Kalimah Khabeethah
Universal reflections on the blessing of security and the Ka'bah

name: Al-Hijr
historical_context: Revealed around the transition from secret dawah to open public preaching in Mecca; guarantees the eternal preservation of the Qur'an (*Inna nahnu nazzalna adh-dhikr*).
key_events: The divine mandate: "Fasda' bima tu'mar wa a'rid 'an al-mushrikeen"
Consolation for the Prophet's constricted chest through Sujood

name: An-Nahl
historical_context: The Surah of Blessings (Ni'am). Contains critical ayah-level occasions: Ammar ibn Yasir uttering kufr under torture while his heart remained firm in faith, and the post-Uhud grief over Hamzah.
key_events: Descent of "Illa man ukriha wa qalbuhu mutma'innun bil-iman" for Ammar
Descent of "Wa in 'aqabtum fa-'aqiboo bi-mithli ma 'ooqibtum bih" (Patience over vengeance)

name: Al-Isra
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 125 (Rabbis Questioning Concerning the Soul / Ar-Ruh)
historical_context: Framed by the Night Journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and ascent through the heavens. Passages triggered by Jewish rabbis prompting Quraysh to interrogate the Prophet about the Soul.
key_events: Ibn Mas'ud walking with the Prophet in Medina when rabbis demanded: "Tell us of the Soul!"
Prophet leaning upon a palm branch as revelation descended: "Qul ar-roohu min amri Rabbi"

name: Al-Kahf
primary_hadith_sources: Sirah Ibn Ishaq; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Vol. 5, p. 135
historical_context: Quraysh dispatched An-Nadr ibn al-Harith and 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt to Jewish rabbis of Medina. The rabbis formulated three litmus tests: the youths who vanished, the world traveler, and the Soul.
key_events: The Prophet's omission of "In sha' Allah" causing revelation to pause for 15 days
The four trial narratives revealed resolving the rabbinical challenges

name: Maryam
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4732 (Al-'As ibn Wa'il Refusing Debt to Khabbab)
historical_context: Recited by Ja'far ibn Abi Talib before the Negus of Abyssinia. Specific verses triggered by the arrogance of Al-'As ibn Wa'il refusing to pay a blacksmith debt to Khabbab.
key_events: Al-'As mocking Khabbab: "I will pay you when I die and receive my wealth and sons in Heaven!"
Descent of "Afa-ra'ayta alladhee kafara bi-ayatina wa qala la-ootayanna malan wa walada"

name: Ta-Ha
historical_context: Early Meccan revelation reassuring the Prophet that revelation was not sent to cause him distress (*Li-tashqa*); famously read by Umar ibn al-Khattab precipitating his conversion to Islam.
key_events: Spontaneous revelation comforting the Prophet during exhausting night vigils
The epic theophany of Moses at the burning bush in Mount Tuwa

name: Al-Anbiya
historical_context: Meccan doxology of prophetic trials (Abraham, Job, Jonah, Zechariah); contains specific passages answering pagan polemics regarding idolaters and objects of worship.
key_events: Abdullah ibn az-Ziba'ra arguing that if idols enter Hell, Jesus and angels must too
Descent of "Inna alladheena sabaqat lahum minna al-husna ula'ika 'anha mub'adoon"

name: Al-Hajj
historical_context: Transitional revelation between Mecca and Medina, addressing the cataclysmic earthquake of the Hour, Abrahamic Hajj, and the historic military charter of self-defense.
key_events: Ali swearing that "Hadhani khasmani" was revealed for the Badr duelists (Ali, Hamzah, Ubaydah)
The historic first permission to take up arms: "Udhina lilladheena yuqataloona bi-annahum zulimoo"

name: Al-Mu'minun
historical_context: Revealed spontaneously in Mecca as the definitive constitution of spiritual triumph (*Falah*), Khushu' in prayer, sexual modesty, and seven stations of morphogenesis.
key_events: Spontaneous descent opening with "Qad aflaha al-mu'minoon"
Umar narrating the Prophet receiving revelation with bee-like humming

name: An-Nur
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4750 (The Epic Slander / Hadith al-Ifk)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4747 (Statute of Li'an / Hilal ibn Umayyah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4759 (Abu Bakr's Pardon of Mistah)
historical_context: Revealed around 5-6 AH to protect communal purity, establishing laws of chastity, domestic privacy, the Light of Allah, and vindicating the Mother of the Believers 'A'ishah.
key_events: Hadith al-Ifk: 'A'ishah's month of illness, tears, and ten verses of divine vindication
Hilal ibn Umayyah accusing his wife, triggering the solemn five-oath procedure of Li'an
Abu Bakr swearing to cut financial support to Mistah, and divine order: "Wa la ya'tali ulul-fadli"

name: Al-Furqan
historical_context: The Sovereign Criterion. Contains the famous historical occasion of 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt apostatizing to please his companion Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
key_events: 'Uqbah hosting a banquet, reciting the Shahadah to please the Prophet, then retracting it
Descent of "Wa yawma ya'addu adh-dhalimu 'ala yadayh ya laytani ittakhadhtu ma'a ar-rasooli sabeela"

name: Ash-Shu'ara
historical_context: Chronicles the prophetic refrain (*Inni lakum rasoolun ameen*); concluded by verses addressing pagan poets spreading satire, and exempting righteous believing poets.
key_events: Believing poets (Hassan, Ibn Rawahah, Ka'b) weeping when "The poets are followed by deviants" descended
Descent of the saving exception: "Illa alladheena amanoo wa 'amiloo as-salihati wa dhakaroo Allaha katheera"

name: An-Naml
historical_context: Spontaneous Meccan revelation detailing the divine gifts of wisdom granted to David and Solomon, the compassionate Ant, the Hoopoe, Bilqis, and Thamud; no verified worldly sabab.
key_events: Spontaneous revelation of Solomon's letter: "Innahu min Sulaymana wa innahu Bismillahi ar-Rahmani ar-Rahim"
Cosmic demonstration of mountains passing like clouds

name: Al-Qasas
historical_context: Chronicles the early life of Moses, the Nile basket, and Qarun's collapse; features the heartbreaking deathbed of the Prophet's protective uncle Abu Talib in Mecca.
key_events: The Prophet pleading with dying Abu Talib: "O uncle, say La ilaha illa Allah, a word I can argue for you before Allah!"
Abu Jahl pressing Abu Talib to die on the religion of his fathers
Descent of "Innaka la tahdi man ahbabta wa lakinna Allaha yahdi man yashaa'"

name: Al-Ankabut
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih Muslim 1748 (Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas & His Mother)
historical_context: The Crucible of Testing (Fitnah). Contains the personal trial of young Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas whose mother staged a life-threatening hunger strike under the sun to force his apostasy.
key_events: Sa'd telling his mother: "If you had 100 souls dying one by one, I would never leave Islam!"
Descent of "Wa in jahadaka li-tushrika bee ma laysa laka bihi 'ilmun fala tuti'huma"

name: Ar-Rum
primary_hadith_sources: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3193 (Abu Bakr's Wager with Quraysh)
historical_context: Revealed around 615 CE when Persian armies defeated Byzantine Christians, delighting pagan Quraysh. Allah prophesied Byzantine victory within 3-9 years (*Bid'i Sineen*), synchronized with Badr.
key_events: Abu Bakr wagering 100 camels with Ubayy ibn Khalaf on Byzantine resurgence
Byzantine counter-offensive victory verifying the prophecy to the letter

name: Luqman
historical_context: Sagehood, parental honor, and the mustard seed; opened by the condemnation of An-Nadr ibn al-Harith who imported foreign Persian folklore and singing girls to drown out the Qur'an.
key_events: An-Nadr declaring: "Muhammad tells tales of 'Ad and Thamud; I tell tales of Rustam and Isfandiyar!"
Descent of "Wa mina an-nasi man yashtaree lahwa al-hadithi li-yudilla 'an sabeelillahi bi-ghayri 'ilm"

name: As-Sajdah
historical_context: Revealed spontaneously in Mecca as an existential awakening detailing the 1,000-year day, creation from clay, night vigils (Tatajafa), and resurrection; instituted as the canonical Friday dawn recitation.
key_events: The Prophet's invariable practice of reciting the entire surah every Friday dawn
Bedtime recitation paired with Surah Al-Mulk protecting against punishment

name: Al-Ahzab
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4785 (The Siege of the 10,000 Confederates)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4787 (Marriage to Zaynab & Abolition of Adoption)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4790 (Ayat al-Takhyir / The Wives' Ultimatum)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3211 (Umm Salamah & The Spiritual Decalogue)
historical_context: Revealed in 5 AH arbitrating five monumental crises: the 10,000 Confederate Trench Siege, the abolition of adoption taboos through Zaynab's marriage, the Prophet's household standards, and outer modesty (Jilbab).
key_events: The 10,000 Confederate siege of Medina, freezing winter, and miraculous routing wind
Marriage of the Prophet to Zaynab bint Jahsh shattering pre-Islamic adoption taboos
Ayat al-Takhyir giving the Mothers of the Believers the choice between dunya and Allah
Ayat al-Hijab descending during the wedding banquet of Zaynab

name: Saba
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4701 (Archangels Prostrating at Divine Speech)
historical_context: Spontaneous Meccan discourse on cosmic ownership, the weight of an atom (Mithqala Dharrah), Dawud's singing mountains, Sulayman's staff demystifying Jinn, and the flood of Ma'rib (Sayl al-'Arim).
key_events: Spontaneous revelation celebrating the House of David's gratitude
Archangels trembling like chains on stone when divine revelation is spoken

name: Fatir
primary_hadith_sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3232 (Prophetic Vision of Gabriel's 600 Wings)
historical_context: Spontaneous Meccan revelation praising the Originator of the heavens and earth, detailing multi-winged angels, the date-seed membrane (Qitmeer), human Faqr, and the three heirs of the Book.
key_events: Spontaneous celebration of creation ex nihilo and angelic hierarchies
The three chosen classes of the Ummah inheriting the Book entering 'Adn

name: Ya-Sin
historical_context: Revealed in Mecca regarding the denial of bodily resurrection by pagan chieftains, with pivotal Medina verses addressing Banu Salimah's mosque relocation.
key_events: Prophet commands Banu Salimah to keep outer borders populated: footsteps are recorded (Ayah 12)
Ubayy ibn Khalaf crumbles rotten bone in Prophet's face asking who revives it (Ayat 77-79)

name: As-Saffat
historical_context: Demolishes pagan myths of angelic daughters and jinn lineage while confirming prophetic perseverance and celestial defense.
key_events: Demons eavesdropping struck by piercing meteors (Shihabun Thaqib, Ayat 6-10)
Prophet institutes concluding triadic praise after prayer and gatherings (Ayat 180-182)

name: Sad
asbab_label: Abu Talib Bedside Council & Dawud Sujood
status_label: Abu Talib Bedside Council & High Council Debate
historical_context: Triggered by Quraysh elders attempting to force a diplomatic compromise at Abu Talib's deathbed, rejecting monotheism.
key_events: Abu Jahl and chieftains reject La ilaha illallah at Abu Talib's deathbed (Ayat 1-5)
Prophet explains the archangels' debate over great expiations (Kaffarat, Ayah 69)

name: Az-Zumar
historical_context: Revealed to invite desperate sinners back to hope and divine forgiveness, while establishing Allah's absolute sovereign majesty.
key_events: Polytheists guilty of murder and adultery ask if redemption is possible: Ayah 53 revealed
Rabbi describes creation on God's Fingers; Prophet confirms with Ayah 67

name: Ghafir
asbab_label: Abu Bakr Ka'bah Defense & Du'a is Worship
status_label: Abu Bakr Ka'bah Defense & Du'a is Worship
historical_context: Opens the seven Hawameem, reassuring persecuted believers through the courtroom drama of Pharaoh's secret believer.
key_events: Abu Bakr rescues Prophet being strangled at Ka'bah quoting Ayah 28
Prophet explains supplication is the very essence of worship (Ayah 60)

name: Fussilat
historical_context: Revealed during intensified Meccan diplomatic pressure and theological debate concerning divine omniscience.
key_events: Utbah offers kingship and gold; Prophet recites Fussilat until Utbah begs him to stop at Ayah 13
Three men whisper at Ka'bah debating if Allah hears: Ayah 22 revealed

name: Ash-Shura
historical_context: Establishes institutional consultation and reminds Quraysh of the bonds of womb uniting them with the Prophet.
key_events: Prophet asks for familial affection and cessation of hostility from Quraysh (Ayah 23)
Consultation codified as fundamental ethical pillar alongside prayer and charity (Ayah 38)

name: Az-Zukhruf
historical_context: Exposes the fallacy of measuring divine favor by worldly riches, while sanctifying human travel through prayer.
key_events: Meccan and Ta'if magnates protest why Qur'an was not given to their billionaires (Ayah 31)
Prophet institutes the universal riding supplication upon mounting transports (Ayat 13-14)

name: Ad-Dukhan
historical_context: Severe famine strikes pagan Makkah until skies appear smoky, leading to pleas for relief and warning of Badr.
key_events: Prophet prays for famine like Yusuf's seven years; skies fill with smoke of hunger (Ayat 10-16)
Abu Sufyan pleads for relief, promising belief; reverts once rain falls

name: Al-Jathiyah
historical_context: Final Hawameem, refuting ancient and modern materialists who attribute decay to time, while commanding patience.
key_events: Prophet transmits Hadith Qudsi forbidding the cursing of time (Ad-Dahr, Ayah 24)
Command given to believers to exercise strategic forgiveness toward pagan insults in Mecca (Ayah 14)

name: Al-Ahqaf
status_label: Jinn Delegation at Nakhlah & Filial Piety
historical_context: Revealed in Mecca following the Prophet's difficult journey to Ta'if, recording the jinn listening to prayer at Batn Nakhlah and Abu Bakr's family embracing Islam.
key_events: Delegation of seven jinn from Nisibin listen in silence to the Qur'an at Batn Nakhlah and return as monotheistic preachers (Ayat 29-32)
Honoring parents and the 40th year supplication revealed concerning Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (Ayah 15)

name: Muhammad
historical_context: Revealed in Medina legislating ethical combat, the binding of prisoners, and exposing Medinan hypocrites who mocked prophetic sermons.
key_events: Charter of war captives: grace or ransom without torture (Ayah 4)
Hypocrites mocked the Prophet's Friday khutbah upon leaving the mosque: What did he say just now? (Ayah 16)

name: Al-Fath
status_label: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah & Bay'at ar-Ridwan
historical_context: Revealed on the return march from the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah in Dhu'l-Qa'dah 6 AH, proclaiming the peaceful truce as a manifest victory.
key_events: Descent of Inna Fatahna Laka Fathan Mubeena at Kura' al-Ghamim (Ayat 1-3)
Bay'at ar-Ridwan pledge under the tree when Uthman was detained in Makkah (Ayat 10, 18)

name: Al-Hujurat
historical_context: Revealed in Medina codifying social ethics, fact-checking rumors (Fatabayyanoo), and abolishing racial supremacy at the Conquest of Makkah.
key_events: Al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah rumor regarding Banu al-Mustaliq investigated and dismissed: Fatabayyanoo! (Ayah 6)
Banu Tamim shouting from behind the private rooms of the Prophet (Ayat 4-5)
Universal declaration of human equality revealed when Bilal proclaimed the Adhan atop the Ka'bah (Ayah 13)

name: Qaf
status_label: Friday Minbar Liturgy & Rebuttal of Sabbath Fatigue
historical_context: Early Meccan revelation chosen by the Prophet for weekly Friday sermon recitations, refuting the myth that God rested on the Sabbath.
key_events: Prophet recited Surah Qaf every Friday on the minbar during Khutbah (Sahih Muslim 873)
Rebutting Jewish claim that God rested on Saturday: Wa ma massana min lughoob (Ayah 38)

name: Adh-Dhariyat
status_label: Bedouin Weeping at Guaranteed Sustenance & Li-Ya'budoon
historical_context: Meccan revelation establishing cosmic expansion, the guarantee of livelihood, and the ultimate purpose of human and jinn existence.
key_events: Bedouin weeping at the divine oath guaranteeing sustenance in heaven: Fees-sama'i rizqukum (Ayat 22-23)
Promulgation of the grand ontological charter of worship: Li-ya'budoon (Ayah 56)

name: At-Tur
status_label: Jubayr ibn Mut'im's Conversion & The Maghrib Recitation
historical_context: Revealed in Mecca, containing the four piercing philosophical inquests that shook the pagan chieftain Jubayr ibn Mut'im during Maghrib prayer.
key_events: Jubayr ibn Mut'im hearing the four inquests (Were they created from nothing?) in Maghrib prayer leading to his conversion (Ayat 35-37)
The tender reassurance to the Prophet in Mecca: Fa-innaka bi-a'yunina (Ayah 48)

name: An-Najm
status_label: First Public Prostration (Sujood) in Islamic History
historical_context: The first surah publicly recited with an ayah of prostration in Makkah, detailing the Prophet's ascension to Sidrat al-Muntaha.
key_events: The monumental first collective prostration in Makkah where even pagan polytheists fell into Sujood (Ayah 62)
Vindication of prophetic sight at Sidrat al-Muntaha: Ma zagha al-basaru wa ma tagha (Ayat 13-18)

name: Al-Qamar
status_label: Splitting of the Moon & The Badr Coalition Defeat
historical_context: Meccan revelation witnessing the visible physical splitting of the moon over Mount Abu Qubays and Mount Hira.
key_events: The moon split into two distinct halves in response to Quraysh challenge (Ayat 1-2)
The prophecy of the defeat of the coalition fulfilled years later at Badr: Sa-yuhzamu al-jam'u (Ayah 45)

name: Ar-Rahman
status_label: Recitation to the Jinn Council & 31 Refrains
historical_context: Known as the Bride of the Qur'an ('Aroos al-Qur'an), recited by the Prophet to the jinn council on the Night of the Jinn.
key_events: Prophet recites to the jinn who responded with praise to all 31 refrains: There is nothing of Your favors we deny! (Ayat 13-78)
Declaration of the mortality of all finite creation: Kullu man 'alayha fan (Ayat 26-27)

name: Al-Waqi'ah
historical_context: Revealed in Mecca deconstructing materialist denial of resurrection with the tripartite division of humanity.
key_events: Companions weeping over the fewness of the Foremost, followed by divine comfort for the Right Hand
The grand oath by stellar descents

name: Al-Hadid
historical_context: The inaugural Musabbihat Surah integrating cosmic theology with the demand for financial sacrifice and industrial strength.
key_events: Ibn Mas'ud's testimony that barely 4 years after Islam Allah admonished their hearts
Abu ad-Dahdah donating his 600-palm orchard as a Goodly Loan

name: Al-Mujadilah
historical_context: Revealed in Medina dismantling pagan Zihar following Khawlah bint Tha'labah's tearful dispute before the Prophet.
key_events: Allah hearing Khawlah's whispers above seven heavens
The three-tiered Kaffarah instituted
Making room in Friday assemblies for Badr veterans

name: Al-Hashr
historical_context: Revealed in 4 AH chronicling the bloodless surrender and banishment of Banu an-Nadir from Medina.
key_events: Ibn Abbas designating the chapter Surat an-Nadir
Cutting date palms sanctioned by divine leave
Altruism of the Ansar who preferred guests over hungry children

name: Al-Mumtahanah
historical_context: Revealed preceding the Conquest of Mecca, regulating political allegiances, benevolence to peaceful non-combatants, and testing female refugees.
key_events: Interception of Hatib's letter at Rawdat Khakh
Asma' maintaining ties with her pagan mother
The six moral pillars of the Women's Allegiance

name: As-Saff
historical_context: Revealed in Medina rebuking verbal bravado and establishing disciplined solidarity like a lead-cemented wall.
key_events: Companions wishing to know the most beloved deed, then wavering when sacrifice was revealed
Jesus heralding Ahmad as the final apostle

name: Al-Jumu'ah
historical_context: Codifying the weekly Friday congregational liturgy and rebuking commercial distractions during the sermon.
key_events: Dihyah's food caravan arriving during Friday Khutbah, leaving only twelve companions standing
Prophecy that Persians would attain faith even at the Pleiades

name: Al-Munafiqun
historical_context: Revealed after the Expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq exposing the sedition of Abdullah ibn Ubayy and vindicating young Zayd ibn Arqam.
key_events: Ibn Ubayy's boast that the mighty would expel the humiliated
Divine vindication of young Zayd ibn Arqam
Dying soul's desperate plea for respite to give charity

name: At-Taghabun
historical_context: Revealing the Day of Mutual Disillusion (At-Taghabun) and providing guidance when family affection hinders spiritual duty.
key_events: Meccan families clinging to husbands to prevent migration, followed by divine command to pardon
The guided heart in calamity
The Goodly Loan multiplied

name: At-Talaq
historical_context: Known as Minor An-Nisa, standardizing ethical divorce, housing rights during 'Iddah, and guaranteeing deliverance for the God-conscious.
key_events: Ibn Umar divorcing during menses, commanded to reconcile
Ubayy asking about non-menstruating and pregnant women
The golden axiom of deliverance

name: At-Tahrim
historical_context: Revealed in Medina resolving a domestic crisis in the prophetic household and presenting four archetypal women of world history.
key_events: The secret vow regarding honey at Zaynab's apartment
The breach of confidence unmasked by revelation
The celestial coalition defending the Prophet
Wives of Noah/Lot vs Asiya/Maryam

name: Al-Mulk
historical_context: Opens Juz Tabarak with proofs of divine sovereignty and safeguards against the trial of the grave.
key_events: Pagans whispering secretly, Ayah 13 revealed on divine omniscience
Prophetic designation of 30-verse surah interceding for its companion

name: Al-Qalam
historical_context: Second revelation in chronological order, defending prophetic character against Meccan allegations of madness.
key_events: Exoneration of the Prophet from charges of possession by the oath of the Pen
Branding the snout of Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah for slander
Parable of the Blighted Orchard

name: Al-Haqqah
status_label: The Inevitable Reality & Umar's Ka'bah Awakening
historical_context: Delineating the terrifying reality of the Day of Sorting and the preservation of scripture against human interference.
key_events: Umar eavesdropping on the Prophet at Ka'bah, thoughts refuted in real-time
The divine pledge to sever the life-artery if scripture were fabricated

name: Al-Ma'arij
historical_context: Revealed when Meccan oligarchs demanded immediate catastrophe if the prophetic warning was truthful.
key_events: An-Nadr ibn al-Harith invoking stones from heaven, Ayah 1 revealed
Portrait of human impatience except for steadfast devotees of prayer

name: Nuh
status_label: Genealogy of Idolatry & 950 Years of Da'wah
historical_context: Consoling the Prophet in Mecca by detailing Noah's monumental perseverance and the deception behind idol worship.
key_events: Ibn Abbas explaining how statues of righteous men became Arabian idols
Noah's strategic counsel to seek forgiveness for rain, wealth, and offspring

name: Al-Jinn
status_label: The Valley of Nakhlah & The Barred Heavens
historical_context: Revealed upon return from Ta'if, when Jinn heard the Prophet reciting at Nakhlah and immediately embraced faith.
key_events: Meteors preventing demonic eavesdropping, leading Jinn to discover the Qur'an
Abolition of taking refuge in Jinn and spirits

name: Al-Muzzammil
status_label: The Mandatory Night Vigil & Gracious Abrogation
historical_context: Foundational spiritual training camp establishing night prayer, later eased after one full year.
key_events: One year of obligatory night vigil until companions' feet swelled
Ayah 20 revealed easing obligation to whatever is easy from the Qur'an

name: Al-Muddaththir
status_label: The Resumption of Wahy & Al-Walid's Deliberation
historical_context: Resumption of revelation ending the pause, commanding public warning and addressing elite Meccan conspiracies.
key_events: The Prophet seeing Jibril between heaven and earth, returning to be cloaked
Al-Walid crafting the charge of 'inherited magic', condemned to Saqar

name: Al-Qiyamah
status_label: Tongue Haste Protocol & The Rebuilt Fingertips
historical_context: Establishing the divine memorization protocol for the Qur'an and affirming physical resurrection down to fingertips.
key_events: Prophet moving lips rapidly in fear of forgetting, commanded to listen quietly
Adi ibn Rabi'ah questioning bodily resurrection, answered by rebuilt fingertips

name: Al-Insan
status_label: Feeding the Captive for Allah & Resisting Compromise
historical_context: Celebrating supreme selfless altruism in Medina and demanding patience against corrupt worldly bribes.
key_events: Righteous household feeding destitute, orphan, and captive purely for Allah's Face
Command to refuse compromise with worldly sinners and persevere in morning/evening worship

name: Al-Mursalat
status_label: Cave of Mina Descent & The Escaping Serpent
historical_context: Revealed fresh in a cave in Mina, concluding Juz Tabarak with cosmic oaths and the tenfold warning refrain.
key_events: Ibn Mas'ud witnessing the revelation in the cave of Mina as a serpent slipped away
The tenfold judicial refrain indicting those who deny the divine message
